units.title: Integrating a backward exponential derivative bound
units.statement: A scalar interpolation starting at zero inherits the exact endpoint bound obtained by integrating its backward exponential derivative majorant.
assumptions: H has derivative H' at every point of [0,t].
The displayed upper derivative bound holds for 0<s<t.
q and E are arbitrary real scalars; their required order information is already encoded in the derivative inequality.

steps.title: Build the exact comparison primitive
steps.text: Define B(s) from the integrated exponential kernel so that B(0)=0 and B'(s)=q e^{-r(t-s)}E.
steps.lean: Differentiate Real.exp and cancel r using r>0.

steps.title: Compare derivatives
steps.text: The assumed bound gives (B-H)'≥0, hence B-H is monotone on [0,t].

steps.title: Evaluate both endpoints
steps.text: At zero both functions vanish; evaluating B at t gives the exact convolution factor.
steps.lean: Use Real.exp_zero and normalize the endpoint algebra.

units.lean_statement: All scalar quantities, interval scopes, and endpoint hypotheses are explicit.
units.lean_proof: The proof differentiates the exact comparison primitive and applies Mathlib's derivative monotonicity theorem.
units.boundary: This is the real-analysis leaf after a semigroup has supplied its entropy-production and gradient-contraction estimates.
